text:
Setting clear project goals is essential for success, and using the SMART framework is a great starting point. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase mobile page speed by 20% within three months."

Once your goals are set, break them into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should lead to a clear deliverable, such as a report or a prototype, which you can review and share.

Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment. Everyone involved—from team members to clients—should understand and agree on the goals. Regular communication keeps everyone on the same page, reducing confusion and making collaboration smoother. With clear goals, milestones, and teamwork, your project has a much higher chance of success.
